last_transition_reason: The proof is correct and complete. It partitions X into the zero-labeled set Z and one-labeled set O, enumerates them as Z = {z_1,...,z_n} and O = {o_1,...,o_m} with n >= m by hypothesis, pairs each o_i with z_i, and fixes the remaining zeros. The resulting map is total, well-defined, involutive, flips labels on every moved point, and has only zero-labeled fixed points. This matches the lemma statement exactly and uses no undeclared or forbidden dependencies.
latest_nl_proof:
Let
Z := {x in X : p(x) = 0}
and
O := {x in X : p(x) = 1}.
Because p maps X into {0,1}, every element of X lies in exactly one of Z or O. Thus X = Z ∪ O and Z ∩ O = ∅.

Since X is finite, the subsets Z and O are finite. Write
O = {o_1, ..., o_m},
Z = {z_1, ..., z_n},
for some integers m,n >= 0. The hypothesis says that the number of zero-labeled elements is at least the number of one-labeled elements, so n >= m.

Now define a map iota : X -> X as follows:
- for 1 <= i <= m, set iota(o_i) = z_i;
- for 1 <= i <= m, set iota(z_i) = o_i;
- for m < j <= n, set iota(z_j) = z_j.

This is well-defined because O and Z are disjoint, and every element of X is either some o_i or some z_j.

We check that iota is an involution.
- If x = o_i with 1 <= i <= m, then iota(iota(x)) = iota(z_i) = o_i = x.
- If x = z_i with 1 <= i <= m, then iota(iota(x)) = iota(o_i) = z_i = x.
- If x = z_j with m < j <= n, then iota(iota(x)) = iota(z_j) = z_j = x.
Hence iota(iota(x)) = x for every x in X.

Next, suppose iota(x) != x. Then x is in one of the first two cases above.
- If x = o_i, then iota(x) = z_i, so
  p(iota(x)) = p(z_i) = 0 = 1 - 1 = 1 - p(o_i) = 1 - p(x).
- If x = z_i with 1 <= i <= m, then iota(x) = o_i, so
  p(iota(x)) = p(o_i) = 1 = 1 - 0 = 1 - p(z_i) = 1 - p(x).
Thus whenever iota(x) != x, we have p(iota(x)) = 1 - p(x).

Finally, if iota(x) = x, then x cannot be any o_i and cannot be any z_i with 1 <= i <= m; therefore x = z_j for some j with m < j <= n. Hence p(x) = 0.

So iota is an involution on X, every moved point is matched with a point of opposite label, and every fixed point has label 0. This is exactly the required conclusion.

statement_nl: Let X be a finite set, and let p : X -> {0,1} be a function. Assume that the number of elements x in X with p(x) = 0 is at least the number of elements x in X with p(x) = 1. Then there exists a map iota : X -> X such that iota(iota(x)) = x for every x in X, and such that: if iota(x) != x, then p(iota(x)) = 1 - p(x); and if iota(x) = x, then p(x) = 0.

domain_restrictions: p must assign each element of X either 0 or 1
the count of zero-labeled elements of X is at least the count of one-labeled elements of X
iota is a total function from X to X
iota is an involution on X
every fixed point of iota must be labeled 0
every non-fixed point must be paired with an element of the opposite label
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For any finite set X equipped with a binary labeling p, if there are at least as many zeros as ones, then X can be partitioned by an involution iota so that every moved point is matched with a point of the opposite label, and every fixed point has label 0.
quantifier_order: for every function p from X to {0,1}
if the number of x in X with p(x)=0 is at least the number of x in X with p(x)=1
then there exists a function iota from X to X
such that for every x in X, iota applied twice to x equals x
and for every x in X, if iota(x) is not x then p(iota(x)) equals 1 minus p(x)
and for every x in X, if iota(x) equals x then p(x) equals 0

witness_dependencies: The witness iota depends on both X and p
For each x, the value iota(x) is determined globally by the chosen iota, not by x alone
The condition on non-fixed points depends on the paired element iota(x) and the label p(x)
There is no separate existential witness for each x; the statement requires one single global iota
